questions.stem: A relation from $X=\{-1, 1, 2\}$ to $Y=\{2, 4, 6\}$ is made of ordered pairs $(a, b)$ with $a \in X$ first and $b \in Y$ second. Tap every ordered pair that could belong to a relation from $X$ to $Y$ (all of $X \times Y$).

canonical_solution.text_md: A relation from X to Y is written with ordered pairs (a, b): the first member a comes from X and the second member b from Y.
Pair each member of X with every member of Y: with -1 we get (-1, 2), (-1, 4), (-1, 6).
These 9 pairs form X × Y; any relation from X to Y, such as the pairs where b = 2a + 4, is chosen from among them.

misconceptions.label: Writes the pairs from Y to X instead of from X to Y
misconceptions.description: The student writes each ordered pair with the book type first and the student second, or draws the arrows from the books back to the students.
